name: accidental-in-essential
summary: An essential record whose title or lead text names technology its kind of record has no business with: a mechanism of an interface or of storage, a technical kind, one of the product's interfaces, or a word the product lists as technology.
explanation: Essential complexity is what any correct solution has to capture, however it is built, so an essential record says what the product's people need in their own words and leaves how it is built to the patterns and the technical specification (LA-STD-PRINCIPLES). The check reads each essential record's title and lead text (its statement, goal, meaning or description), in any letter case, as whole words, singular or plural, code in backticks included, for the words of its kind's group. The domain model, use cases, flows and every other essential kind are read for the interface words page, screen, button, click, endpoint, route, URL, HTTP and query string; the storage words table, row, column, JSON, SQL and database; the titles of the product's own interfaces (such as CLI or Web app); and the technical kinds. A step only one interface can do (a variant) names that interface, so the interface's own title is the step's. A view and its requirements are on their interface by nature, so pages, screens, buttons, clicks, rows, columns, tables, routes and URLs are theirs: they are read for endpoint, HTTP, query string, JSON, SQL, database and the technical kinds. An interface, an integration and an API requirement are a contract with the outside world, which names its mechanism: they are read for the technical kinds only. Patterns, their rules and slots are where the product decides its accidental complexity once, and a test says how it proves through the interface it drives, so neither is read. The technical kinds are data store, repository, data model, value type, event type, projection, command handler, query handler, event handler, endpoint handler, adapter, entry point and UI component. A word that is the title of a term of any of the record's product's domains is the product's language, not technology, so it is not reported: a product has one language, and a term means the same in every domain, so a product about specs has a term Table its every stage may use. The words the product's settings list as technology (technology_words) are read in every group and never excused. A mixed kind, one whose records hold both, is split rather than excused. A write that adds such a record, or changes its title or lead text, is refused for the same words in the text it sets (essential-names-technology): an add's title and lead text, a change's only where it changes them, so a record whose title names a word the owner accepts can still have its lead text changed. This check reads every text of every record, so it reports what was in the data before and what no write has set since. Say what is needed without the mechanism, move the mechanism to the pattern or technical record that decides it, or split the record.
query:
WITH grouped AS (
  SELECT t.id, t.kind, t.lead_column, s.product_id, s.domain_id, g.word_group AS grp,
         lower(t.title) AS title, lower(coalesce(t.lead, '')) AS lead,
         lower(si.title) AS own_interface
  FROM record_text t
  JOIN record_complexity x ON x.id = t.id AND x.complexity = 'essential'
  JOIN essential_word_group g ON g.kind = t.kind
  JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = t.id
  LEFT JOIN flow_step st ON st.id = t.id
  LEFT JOIN interface si ON si.id = st.interface_id
),
lathe_words (grp, word) AS (SELECT word_group, word FROM essential_word),
places AS (SELECT DISTINCT product_id, domain_id, grp FROM grouped),
product_terms AS (
  SELECT d.product_id, lower(trim(tm.title)) AS word
  FROM domain d JOIN term tm ON tm.domain_id = d.id
),
words AS (
  SELECT pl.product_id, pl.domain_id, pl.grp, w.word
  FROM places pl JOIN lathe_words w ON w.grp = pl.grp
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM product_terms o WHERE o.product_id = pl.product_id AND o.word = w.word)
  UNION
  SELECT pl.product_id, pl.domain_id, pl.grp, lower(trim(i.title))
  FROM places pl JOIN interface i ON i.product_id = pl.product_id
  WHERE pl.grp = 'model'
  UNION
  SELECT pl.product_id, pl.domain_id, pl.grp, lower(trim(s.w))
  FROM places pl JOIN (SELECT product_id, unnest(technology_words) AS w FROM product_setting) s ON s.product_id = pl.product_id
  WHERE trim(s.w) <> ''
),
patterns AS (
  SELECT product_id, domain_id, grp,
         string_agg(CASE word WHEN 'repository' THEN 'repositor(?:y|ies)' ELSE regexp_escape(word) END, '|' ORDER BY length(word) DESC, word) AS pattern
  FROM words GROUP BY ALL
),
texts AS (
  SELECT g.id, g.kind, g.lead_column, g.product_id, g.domain_id, g.grp, p.pattern,
         CASE WHEN g.own_interface IS NULL THEN g.title ELSE replace(g.title, g.own_interface, ' ') END AS title,
         CASE WHEN g.own_interface IS NULL THEN g.lead ELSE replace(g.lead, g.own_interface, ' ') END AS lead
  FROM grouped g
  JOIN patterns p ON p.product_id = g.product_id AND p.domain_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM g.domain_id AND p.grp = g.grp
),
candidates AS (
  SELECT t.* FROM texts t
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM words w WHERE w.product_id = t.product_id AND w.domain_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM t.domain_id AND w.grp = t.grp
    AND (contains(t.title, CASE w.word WHEN 'repository' THEN 'repositor' ELSE w.word END) OR contains(t.lead, CASE w.word WHEN 'repository' THEN 'repositor' ELSE w.word END)))
),
found AS (
  SELECT id, kind, lead_column,
         nullif(regexp_extract(title, '(^|[^a-z0-9])(' || pattern || ')(e?s)?([^a-z0-9]|$)', 2), '') AS in_title,
         nullif(regexp_extract(lead, '(^|[^a-z0-9])(' || pattern || ')(e?s)?([^a-z0-9]|$)', 2), '') AS in_lead
  FROM candidates
)
SELECT f.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || f.id || ' is essential but names technology: '
       || concat_ws(' and ',
            CASE WHEN in_title IS NOT NULL THEN 'its title says "' || in_title || '"' END,
            CASE WHEN in_lead IS NOT NULL THEN 'its ' || lead_column || ' says "' || in_lead || '"' END)
       || '; say what the product''s people need and leave the mechanism to the pattern or technical record that decides it, or split the record.' AS message
FROM found f JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = f.kind
WHERE in_title IS NOT NULL OR in_lead IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY record

name: accidental-not-accounted-for
summary: An accidental record that is neither derived (a tooling record generates it), provided (it or a record it sits under names its provider), nor a fill of a pattern's slot that serves an essential record; or an engineering standard or rule that nothing provides and no such record follows.
explanation: Essential complexity is decided once, per product; accidental complexity, what comes from the means used to build it, is derived, provided, or a recorded fill at a slot, never free-floating (LA-STD-PRINCIPLES). A record is accidental by its kind (the technical specification), or as an engineering standard and its rules; a test follows what it proves and is not reported. It is accounted for when a tooling record generates it (generates), when it or a record it sits under is provided by something outside the product (provided_by), or when it fills a pattern's slot (fills) and serves an essential record: it builds an essential obligation as coverage counts it, carries out a pattern rule it meets (a generic piece of code: a shared component, an entry point, a build script), implements an essential record it sits under, directly or through other accidental records such as an endpoint (other than its product or domain), persists an essential aggregate (persists), is linked to an essential record by one of the product's own relations, in either direction, measures an essential record such as a business outcome (measured_by: a report or a script that measures it), or has an essential record under it, such as a contract it holds (a test is never the essential record served); a data store serves what is stored in it that serves. An engineering standard and its rules are the rules that code follows, not code, so they fill no slot: a rule is accounted for when a record that is accounted for builds it as coverage counts it (meets), and a standard when one of its rules is, unless it or its standard is provided. A record that meets a rule and is not accounted for is reported on its own, so the rule it meets stays accounted for through the others. Generate it, name its provider, or record the slot it fills and link it to the essential record it serves; code that serves nothing essential is removed. Link the records that follow an engineering rule to it with meets; a rule that nothing follows is removed.
query:
WITH RECURSIVE up (id, above) AS (
  SELECT id, id FROM record_parent
  UNION ALL
  SELECT up.id, p.parent_id FROM up JOIN record_parent p ON p.id = up.above WHERE p.parent_id IS NOT NULL
),
essential AS (
  SELECT c.id FROM record_complexity c JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = c.kind
  WHERE c.complexity = 'essential' AND c.kind NOT IN ('product', 'domain') AND k.stage IS DISTINCT FROM 'test-plan'
),
serving AS (
  SELECT i.impl_id AS id FROM obligation_impl i JOIN record_complexity c ON c.id = i.obligation_id WHERE c.complexity = 'essential'
  UNION
  SELECT up.id FROM up JOIN record_complexity c ON c.id = up.above WHERE up.above <> up.id AND c.complexity = 'essential' AND c.kind NOT IN ('product', 'domain')
  UNION
  SELECT p.source_id FROM persists p JOIN essential e ON e.id = p.target_id
  UNION
  SELECT l.source_id FROM link l JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation JOIN essential e ON e.id = l.target_id WHERE r.product_id IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT l.target_id FROM link l JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation JOIN essential e ON e.id = l.source_id WHERE r.product_id IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT m.target_id FROM measured_by m JOIN essential e ON e.id = m.source_id
  UNION
  SELECT p.parent_id FROM record_parent p JOIN essential e ON e.id = p.id WHERE p.parent_id IS NOT NULL
),
stores AS (
  SELECT d.target_id AS id FROM stored_in d JOIN serving s ON s.id = d.source_id
),
own AS (
  SELECT target_id AS id FROM generates
  UNION
  SELECT up.id FROM up JOIN provided_by p ON p.source_id = up.above
  UNION
  SELECT f.source_id FROM fills f JOIN serving s ON s.id = f.source_id
  UNION
  SELECT f.source_id FROM fills f JOIN stores s ON s.id = f.source_id
),
followed AS (
  SELECT i.obligation_id AS id FROM obligation_impl i JOIN standard_rule r ON r.id = i.obligation_id JOIN own o ON o.id = i.impl_id
),
accounted AS (
  SELECT id FROM own
  UNION
  SELECT id FROM followed
  UNION
  SELECT r.standard_id FROM standard_rule r JOIN followed f ON f.id = r.id
)
SELECT c.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || c.id || ' is accidental complexity nothing accounts for: '
       || CASE WHEN c.kind = 'standard_rule'
               THEN 'nothing provides it, and no record that is accounted for meets it; link the records that follow it with meets, name its provider, or remove it.'
               WHEN c.kind = 'standard'
               THEN 'nothing provides it, and no record that is accounted for meets one of its rules; link the records that follow its rules with meets, name its provider, or remove it.'
               WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fills f WHERE f.source_id = c.id)
               THEN 'it fills a slot but serves no essential record; put it under the essential record it implements, link it to the essential record it serves, or remove it.'
               ELSE 'no tooling record generates it, nothing provides it, and it fills no slot; generate it, name its provider, or record the pattern slot it fills.' END AS message
FROM record_complexity c
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = c.kind
WHERE c.complexity = 'accidental' AND k.stage IS DISTINCT FROM 'test-plan'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM accounted a WHERE a.id = c.id)
ORDER BY record

name: aggregate-too-large
summary: An aggregate with more entities than its product's max_entities_per_aggregate setting.
explanation: The setting is the product's product_setting row (7 when it has none). An aggregate is the smallest cluster of entities that must stay consistent after one command: one transaction changes it, and everything in it is loaded, locked and saved together. Most need a root and a few children; one that holds many entities is usually several clusters that change at different times, held together only by references, so every command pays for all of them and two people's changes clash for no reason. A rule that spans two aggregates is checked by a specification, or followed through an event and a policy. Split it into smaller aggregates that each change together.
query:
WITH sized AS (
  SELECT aggregate_id, count(*) AS n FROM entity GROUP BY aggregate_id
)
SELECT a.id AS record,
       'Aggregate ' || a.id || ' has ' || z.n || ' entities, more than the ' || coalesce(ps.max_entities_per_aggregate, 7)
       || ' that the product''s max_entities_per_aggregate setting allows; split it into smaller aggregates that each change together.' AS message
FROM aggregate a
JOIN sized z ON z.aggregate_id = a.id
JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = a.id
LEFT JOIN product_setting ps ON ps.product_id = s.product_id
WHERE z.n > coalesce(ps.max_entities_per_aggregate, 7)
ORDER BY record

name: domain-named-for-technology
summary: A domain is named for a technology layer or delivery channel rather than a business capability.
explanation: A domain is a vertical slice of business capability: it owns its model, its use cases, their interface design, the technical records that implement them and their tests. Technology is expressed through the technical kinds inside each domain, never as a domain of its own. A domain whose title or domain code (its ID after the product prefix, such as LEND in TL-LEND) names a technology splits one capability across several domains. The words are web app, frontend, front end, backend, back end, API, UI, server, database, DB, desktop, mobile, engine, infrastructure, infra and Electron, matched as whole words in any letter case, with or without a space or hyphen inside the two-word ones, and in the plural. Only the title and code are read, never the description. Name the domain for the capability it serves.
query:
SELECT id AS record,
       'Domain ' || id || ' is named for a technology, not a business capability: '
       || CASE WHEN in_title <> '' THEN 'its title "' || trim(title) || '" says "' || in_title || '"' ELSE '' END
       || CASE WHEN in_title <> '' AND in_code <> '' THEN ' and ' ELSE '' END
       || CASE WHEN in_code <> '' THEN 'its code ' || code || ' says "' || in_code || '"' ELSE '' END
       || '; name the domain for the capability it serves, and make the technology a layer in each domain''s Design stage.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT id, title, code,
         regexp_extract(lower(title), '(^|[^a-z])(' || words || ')([^a-z]|$)', 2) AS in_title,
         regexp_extract(lower(code), '(^|[^a-z])(' || words || ')([^a-z]|$)', 2) AS in_code
  FROM (
    SELECT id, title, CASE WHEN starts_with(id, product_id || '-') THEN substr(id, length(product_id) + 2) ELSE id END AS code
    FROM domain
  ),
  (SELECT 'web[ -]?apps?|front[ -]?ends?|back[ -]?ends?|apis?|uis?|servers?|databases?|dbs?|desktops?|mobile'
          || '|engines?|infrastructure|infra|electron' AS words)
)
WHERE in_title <> '' OR in_code <> ''
ORDER BY record

name: endpoint-route-not-in-file
summary: An endpoint whose handler's file does not name its method and route.
explanation: An endpoint handler serves its endpoint's method and route, so its file names both: the route, written any way routes are written (`/tools/{toolId}`, `/tools/:toolId`, `/tools/<tool-id>`, `/tools/[toolId]`, a template's `${toolId}`, or a regular expression literal that matches it, such as `/^\/tools\/(\d+)$/`), in code, a string or a comment. Parameters match whatever their names, and only the path counts: a query string or fragment is not part of a route. The method is written in capitals, or called as `.post(`, on the route's line or within two lines of it. Then a reader of the record finds the code, and a route changed on one side and not the other is caught. A handler whose file does not exist yet is technical-file-missing instead. Correct the endpoint's method or route, or point its handler at the file that serves it.
query:
SELECT r.record,
       'Endpoint ' || r.record || ' is ' || r.method || ' ' || r.route || ', but its handler''s file ' || r.files
       || ' does not name that route with that method; correct the endpoint, or point its handler at the file that serves it.' AS message
FROM route_facts r
WHERE r.kind = 'endpoint' AND r.files <> '' AND NOT r.found
ORDER BY record

name: entity-unreferenced
summary: A child entity that its aggregate's root does not reach.
explanation: Each child entity is a part of its aggregate's root, so a `has_one` or `has_many` reaches it from the root, directly or through other children of the same aggregate. Link the child from the root or from another child with `has_one` or `has_many`.
query:
WITH RECURSIVE
  roots AS (SELECT aggregate_id, id AS root FROM entity WHERE role = 'root'),
  parts AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT l.source_id AS source, l.target_id AS target
    FROM (SELECT source_id, target_id FROM has_one UNION ALL SELECT source_id, target_id FROM has_many) l
    JOIN entity s ON s.id = l.source_id
    JOIN entity t ON t.id = l.target_id
  ),
  reached (id) AS (
    SELECT root FROM roots
    UNION
    SELECT p.target FROM parts p JOIN reached r ON r.id = p.source
  )
SELECT e.id AS record,
       'Child entity ' || e.id || ' is not reached from ' || e.aggregate_id || '''s root ' || r.root
       || ' by has_one or has_many; link it from ' || r.root || ' or from the child it is a part of.' AS message
FROM entity e
JOIN roots r ON r.aggregate_id = e.aggregate_id
WHERE e.role = 'child' AND e.id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM reached)
ORDER BY record

name: essential-repeated
summary: The same requirement or step statement in three or more use cases or views: a pattern in disguise, decided again in each.
explanation: Essential complexity is decided once, per product (LA-STD-PRINCIPLES-R05): what several use cases or views share is one decision, written once as a rule of a pattern they follow. The check reads each essential UC requirement's and view requirement's statement and each flow step's title, in lower case, with every title of the product's aggregates and entities (singular or plural) read as one placeholder, an and a read alike, and anything but letters, digits and the placeholder read as one space. A statement that reads the same in three or more use cases or views is reported once, on the first of its records by ID, naming them all. Write the statement once as a rule of a pattern, with a setting for what differs, have the use cases follow it, and drop the repeats.
query:
WITH RECURSIVE statements AS (
  SELECT t.id, s.product_id, coalesce(t.lead, t.title) AS original, lower(coalesce(t.lead, t.title)) AS text
  FROM record_text t
  JOIN record_complexity x ON x.id = t.id AND x.complexity = 'essential'
  JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = t.id
  WHERE t.kind IN ('uc_requirement', 'view_requirement', 'flow_step')
),
up (id, above) AS (
  SELECT id, id FROM statements
  UNION ALL
  SELECT up.id, p.parent_id FROM up JOIN record_parent p ON p.id = up.above WHERE p.parent_id IS NOT NULL
),
owner AS (
  SELECT up.id, min(a.id) AS owner_id FROM up JOIN record_parent a ON a.id = up.above WHERE a.kind IN ('use_case', 'view') GROUP BY up.id
),
names AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.product_id, lower(trim(a.title)) AS name FROM aggregate a JOIN domain d ON d.id = a.domain_id
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT d.product_id, lower(trim(e.title)) FROM entity e JOIN aggregate a ON a.id = e.aggregate_id JOIN domain d ON d.id = a.domain_id
),
patterns AS (
  SELECT st.id, string_agg(regexp_escape(n.name), '|' ORDER BY length(n.name) DESC, n.name) AS pattern
  FROM statements st JOIN names n ON n.product_id = st.product_id AND contains(st.text, n.name)
  GROUP BY st.id
),
named AS (
  SELECT st.id, st.product_id, o.owner_id, st.original,
         CASE WHEN n.pattern IS NULL THEN st.text
              ELSE regexp_replace(regexp_replace(st.text, '(^|[^a-z0-9])(' || n.pattern || ')(e?s)?([^a-z0-9]|$)', '\1<name>\4', 'g'),
                                  '(^|[^a-z0-9])(' || n.pattern || ')(e?s)?([^a-z0-9]|$)', '\1<name>\4', 'g') END AS text_named
  FROM statements st JOIN owner o ON o.id = st.id LEFT JOIN patterns n ON n.id = st.id
),
normalized AS (
  SELECT id, product_id, owner_id, original,
         trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(text_named, '(^|[^a-z0-9<])an([^a-z0-9>])', '\1a\2', 'g'), '[^a-z0-9<>]+', ' ', 'g')) AS key
  FROM named
),
repeated AS (
  SELECT product_id, key, min(id) AS first, arg_min(original, id) AS said, count(DISTINCT owner_id) AS owners,
         string_agg(id, ', ' ORDER BY id) AS ids
  FROM normalized
  WHERE key <> ''
  GROUP BY product_id, key
  HAVING count(DISTINCT owner_id) >= 3
)
SELECT first AS record,
       'The same statement, "' || said || '", is said in ' || owners || ' use cases or views (' || ids
       || '): a pattern in disguise; write it once as a rule of a pattern they follow, and drop the repeats.' AS message
FROM repeated
ORDER BY record

name: essential-restates-technical
summary: An essential record that names the shape of a technical record of its product: a table name, a file or folder, an endpoint's route, or a command line.
explanation: What follows from the spec is not essential (LA-STD-PRINCIPLES-R05, R06): a record that says an entity's fields are the rows of a table, or that a check is added with a command line, restates the technical specification in the words of the essential one. The check reads each essential record's title and lead text, but for the kinds that are a contract with the outside world (an interface, an integration, an API requirement), which name their mechanism, and reports what it names exactly: the name of one of the product's tables that holds an underscore, written as storage (followed by row, table or column, singular or plural), unless it is the title of one of the product's terms; a file of one of the product's accidental records, or a folder one of them is in (written with its closing slash); an HTTP method followed by a path, or the route of one of the product's endpoints, in any record but a view and its requirements; and a command line in backticks: a program followed by arguments, one of them a flag (--name or -n) or a placeholder (<name> or %A). It reports only what matches a technical record or that shape, so a word that only sounds technical is never reported. Say what the product's people need in their own words, and leave the shape to the technical record, or remove the record when that is all it says.
query:
WITH texts AS (
  SELECT t.id, t.kind, t.lead_column, s.product_id, g.word_group AS grp, t.title, coalesce(t.lead, '') AS lead
  FROM record_text t
  JOIN record_complexity x ON x.id = t.id AND x.complexity = 'essential'
  JOIN essential_word_group g ON g.kind = t.kind AND g.word_group <> 'surface'
  JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = t.id
),
said AS (
  SELECT id, kind, product_id, grp, 'title' AS col, title AS text FROM texts
  UNION ALL
  SELECT id, kind, product_id, grp, lead_column, lead FROM texts WHERE lead_column IS NOT NULL
),
terms AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.product_id, lower(trim(tm.title)) AS word FROM term tm JOIN domain d ON d.id = tm.domain_id
),
tables AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.product_id, lower(tb.name) AS name FROM "table" tb JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = tb.id WHERE contains(tb.name, '_')
),
files AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.product_id, f.file FROM file_facts f
  JOIN record_complexity x ON x.id = f.record AND x.complexity = 'accidental'
  JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = f.record
),
routes AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.product_id, e.route FROM endpoint e JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = e.id WHERE regexp_matches(e.route, '^/[a-z].*/')
),
found AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.id, a.kind, a.col, 'the table ' || w.token AS shape
  FROM said a, unnest(regexp_extract_all(lower(a.text), '([a-z0-9]+(?:_[a-z0-9]+)+)`? (?:rows?|tables?|columns?)([^a-z0-9]|$)', 1)) w (token)
  JOIN tables tb ON tb.product_id = a.product_id AND tb.name = w.token
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM terms tm WHERE tm.product_id = a.product_id AND tm.word = w.token)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DISTINCT a.id, a.kind, a.col, 'the file ' || w.token
  FROM said a, unnest(regexp_extract_all(a.text, '[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(?:/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)+/?')) w (token)
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM files f WHERE f.product_id = a.product_id AND (f.file = w.token OR (ends_with(w.token, '/') AND starts_with(f.file, w.token))))
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DISTINCT a.id, a.kind, a.col, 'the route ' || w.token
  FROM said a, unnest(regexp_extract_all(a.text, '(?:GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE) /[^ `,;)]*')) w (token)
  WHERE a.grp = 'model'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DISTINCT a.id, a.kind, a.col, 'the route ' || r.route
  FROM said a JOIN routes r ON r.product_id = a.product_id
  WHERE a.grp = 'model' AND contains(a.text, r.route) AND regexp_matches(a.text, '(^|[\s`(])' || regexp_escape(r.route) || '($|[\s`),.;])')
    AND NOT regexp_matches(a.text, '(?:GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE) ' || regexp_escape(r.route))
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DISTINCT a.id, a.kind, a.col, 'the command line ' || w.token
  FROM said a, unnest(regexp_extract_all(a.text, '`([^`]+)`', 1)) w (token)
  WHERE regexp_matches(w.token, '^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]*( +[^ ]+)+$')
    AND regexp_matches(w.token, ' (--?[a-z][a-z0-9-]*|<[a-z][a-z0-9 _-]*>|%[A-Za-z])( |$)')
),
grouped AS (
  SELECT id, kind, string_agg(DISTINCT col, ' and ' ORDER BY col) AS cols, string_agg(DISTINCT shape, ', ' ORDER BY shape) AS shapes
  FROM found GROUP BY id, kind
)
SELECT g.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || g.id || ' restates how it is built: its ' || g.cols || ' names ' || g.shapes
       || ', the shape of a technical record that follows from the spec; say what the product''s people need, or remove the record when that is all it says.' AS message
FROM grouped g JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = g.kind
ORDER BY record

name: event-not-by-outbox
summary: An event a policy hears, whose aggregate is stored in a database table, whose event type is not delivered by outbox.
explanation: An event a policy hears, whose aggregate is stored in a database table (an entity of the aggregate has a table whose storage is `table`), in its own domain or, when published, in another, is delivered by outbox: saved in the same transaction as its aggregate and delivered reliably afterwards, since a lost reaction is a lost change. Its event type records the delivery; one delivered in process, with no delivery given, or no event type at all, leaves the reaction to chance. The rule reads the aggregate's storage because an outbox joins the database transaction that saves the aggregate. Give the event an event type delivered by outbox.
query:
SELECT e.id AS record,
       'Domain event ' || e.id || ' is heard by policy ' || (SELECT string_agg(h.source_id, ', ' ORDER BY h.source_id) FROM hears h WHERE h.target_id = e.id)
       || CASE WHEN t.id IS NULL THEN ', but has no event type; give it one delivered by outbox.'
               WHEN t.delivery IS NULL THEN ', but its event type ' || t.id || ' gives no delivery; deliver it by outbox.'
               ELSE ', but its event type ' || t.id || ' is delivered ' || t.delivery || '; deliver it by outbox.' END AS message
FROM domain_event e
LEFT JOIN event_type t ON t.domain_event_id = e.id
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hears h WHERE h.target_id = e.id)
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "table" tb JOIN entity en ON en.id = tb.entity_id WHERE en.aggregate_id = e.aggregate_id AND tb.storage = 'table')
  AND (t.delivery IS NULL OR t.delivery <> 'outbox')
ORDER BY record

name: event-tense
summary: A domain event's title reads as something that happened, in the past tense.
explanation: An event is named for what happened, such as Loan opened or Payment sent. The check is a heuristic over the title's words, in any letter case and split at anything but a letter: the title passes when its last word, or any word after its first (the word after a one-word subject, as in Loan became overdue), is a past form. A past form is a word of four or more letters ending in "-ed", other than the few such words that are not verbs in the past (need, seed, feed, speed, breed, bleed, embed, proceed, exceed, succeed, hundred, naked, sacred, wicked), or one of the irregular past forms the query lists. The heuristic can miss a past form it does not know, so this is a warning. Name the event in the past tense, as what happened (Tool returned, not Return tool), or add the word to the check's list if it is a past form the check does not know.
query:
SELECT e.id AS record,
       'Event ' || e.id || ' is titled "' || trim(e.title)
       || '", which does not read as past tense; name it for what happened, such as "Loan opened" or "Tool returned".' AS message
FROM domain_event e
WHERE regexp_matches(lower(e.title), '[a-z]')
  AND e.id NOT IN (
    SELECT w.id
    FROM (
      SELECT id, unnest(words) AS word, unnest(generate_series(1, len(words))) AS position, len(words) AS count
      FROM (SELECT id, string_split(trim(regexp_replace(lower(title), '[^a-z]+', ' ', 'g')), ' ') AS words FROM domain_event)
    ) w
    WHERE (w.position > 1 OR w.position = w.count)
      AND (list_contains(string_split(
      'arose arisen ate eaten awoke awoken became begun began bent bound bit bitten blew blown broke broken bred '
      || 'brought built burnt bought caught chose chosen came cost crept cut dealt dug did done drew drawn dreamt '
      || 'drank drunk drove driven fell fallen fed felt fought found fled flew flown forbade forbidden forgot '
      || 'forgotten forgave forgiven froze frozen got gotten gave given went gone grew grown hung had heard hid '
      || 'hidden hit held hurt kept knew known laid led leant learnt left lent let lit lost made meant met mistook '
      || 'mistaken overdone overran overridden overrode overtaken overtook paid put quit read rebuilt redone remade '
      || 'reran rerun reset resent resold retook retaken rewound rewrote rewritten rode ridden rang rung rose risen '
      || 'ran run said saw seen sought sold sent set shook shaken shone shot showed shown shut sang sung sank sunk '
      || 'sat slept slid spoke spoken sped spent spun split spread sprang sprung stood stole stolen stuck struck '
      || 'swore sworn swept swam swum swung took taken taught tore torn told thought threw thrown understood undid '
      || 'undone upheld upset withdrew withdrawn withheld woke woken wore worn won wound wrote written', ' '), w.word)
           OR (length(w.word) >= 4 AND w.word LIKE '%ed' AND NOT list_contains(string_split(
      'need seed feed speed breed bleed embed proceed exceed succeed hundred naked sacred wicked', ' '), w.word)))
  )
ORDER BY record

name: flow-not-offered
summary: A use case with a flow that no interface offers and no integration performs.
explanation: A flow says how its use case is carried out whatever the interface, and each interface that offers the use case has its own version of it. A use case that an outside system carries out on its own, with no person and no interface of the product, is performed by that integration instead. A use case no interface offers and no integration performs has a flow nobody can follow. Offer it through the interfaces it happens through, or have the integration that carries it out perform it.
query:
SELECT f.use_case_id AS record, 'Use case ' || f.use_case_id || ' has a flow, ' || f.id || ', but no interface offers it and no integration performs it; offer it through the interfaces it happens through, or have the integration that carries it out perform it.' AS message
FROM flow f
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offers o WHERE o.target_id = f.use_case_id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM performs p WHERE p.target_id = f.use_case_id)
ORDER BY record

name: flow-title-off-pattern
summary: A flow whose title is not its use case's title.
explanation: A use case has one flow, the same through every interface that offers it, so the flow's title is its use case's: a renamed use case then shows in a flow that still has the old title. The check compares trimmed and in any letter case. Retitle the flow as its use case.
query:
SELECT f.id AS record,
       'Flow ' || f.id || ' is titled "' || trim(f.title) || '", but its use case ' || u.id || ' is "' || trim(u.title) || '"; title it "' || trim(u.title) || '".' AS message
FROM flow f
JOIN use_case u ON u.id = f.use_case_id
WHERE lower(trim(f.title)) <> lower(trim(u.title))
ORDER BY record

name: handoff-not-connected
summary: A handoff step whose policy hears no event the step before it leads to.
explanation: A handoff step carries out a policy: whenever an event, then a command, with the product itself acting (LA-PRD-UC33-R08). It follows the step before it on its path only when its policy hears an event that step leads to: an event raised by the result of the use case before it, when that is a command, or by the command of the policy before it. Steps are compared by path (trimmed, in any letter case) and position. A handoff first on its path, or after a step that carries out nothing yet, is not read; nor is one after a use case with no flow yet, since records are written stage by stage. Link the step to the policy that follows, or have its policy hear the event the step before leads to.
query:
WITH step AS (
  SELECT s.id, s.journey_id, lower(trim(s.path)) AS step_path, s.position, c.target_id AS target
  FROM journey_step s LEFT JOIN carries_out c ON c.source_id = s.id
),
handoff AS (
  SELECT h.id, h.target AS policy, b.id AS before_step, b.target AS before
  FROM step h JOIN policy p ON p.id = h.target
  JOIN step b ON b.journey_id = h.journey_id AND b.step_path = h.step_path AND b.position = h.position - 1
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM flow f WHERE f.use_case_id = b.target) OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM policy q WHERE q.id = b.target)
),
leads AS (
  SELECT h.id, u.result_id AS command FROM handoff h JOIN use_case u ON u.id = h.before JOIN command c ON c.id = u.result_id
  UNION ALL
  SELECT h.id, q.command_id FROM handoff h JOIN policy q ON q.id = h.before
)
SELECT h.id AS record,
       'Journey step ' || h.id || ' hands off to policy ' || h.policy || ', which hears no event that ' || h.before
       || ', carried out by the step before it (' || h.before_step || '), leads to; link the step to the policy that follows '
       || h.before || ', or have ' || h.policy || ' hear the event it raises.' AS message
FROM handoff h
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM leads l JOIN raises r ON r.source_id = l.command JOIN hears e ON e.target_id = r.target_id
  WHERE l.id = h.id AND e.source_id = h.policy
)
ORDER BY record

name: integration-unused
summary: An integration that nothing uses: no flow step or policy exchanges with it, and it provides nothing.
explanation: An integration has no owner: it exists because flow steps or policies exchange with it, or because it provides records of the product from outside it (provided_by), such as a platform or a dependency. One that nothing uses is a leftover, or a link is missing. Link the steps or policies that exchange with it with exchanges_with, name it the provider of what it provides, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'Integration ' || r.id || ' is used by nothing: no flow step or policy exchanges with it and it provides nothing; link the steps or policies that exchange with it with exchanges_with, name it the provider of what it provides, or remove it.' AS message
FROM integration r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM exchanges_with x WHERE x.target_id = r.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM provided_by p WHERE p.target_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: interface-actor-not-the-use-case
summary: An interface that offers a use case none of whose actors uses the interface.
explanation: A step's actor through an interface is the first of its use case's actors that the interface lists among its roles (interface_actor). When the interface lists roles and none of them is one of the use case's actors, nobody can carry the use case out there. List the role among the interface's, add it to the use case's actors, or stop offering the use case through the interface.
query:
SELECT o.source_id AS record,
       'Interface ' || o.source_id || ' offers ' || o.target_id || ', but none of its roles (' || (SELECT string_agg(a.role_name, ', ' ORDER BY a.position) FROM interface_actor a WHERE a.interface_id = o.source_id) || ') is one of the use case''s actors.' AS message
FROM offers o
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM interface_actor a WHERE a.interface_id = o.source_id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM interface_actor a JOIN use_case_actor u ON u.role_name = a.role_name AND u.use_case_id = o.target_id WHERE a.interface_id = o.source_id)
ORDER BY record, o.target_id

name: journey-of-one-use-case
summary: A journey whose steps carry out fewer than two use cases.
explanation: A use case is one role's command or query; a journey strings several of them, with the handoffs between, from a trigger to a result (LA-PRD-UC33-R07). A journey whose steps carry out fewer than two use cases, counting each use case once and each step that carries out nothing yet as a use case still to write, is a use case: its handoffs are that use case's policies. A journey with no step is left to the journey-without-main-path gap. Remove the journey and let its use case serve the outcome through its aggregate or read model, or add the steps it is missing.
query:
WITH counted AS (
  SELECT j.id, count(DISTINCT u.id) + count(s.id) FILTER (WHERE c.target_id IS NULL) AS use_cases, count(s.id) AS steps, min(u.id) AS sole
  FROM journey j
  LEFT JOIN journey_step s ON s.journey_id = j.id
  LEFT JOIN carries_out c ON c.source_id = s.id
  LEFT JOIN use_case u ON u.id = c.target_id
  GROUP BY j.id
)
SELECT id AS record,
       'Journey ' || id || ' carries out ' || CASE WHEN sole IS NULL THEN 'no use case' ELSE 'one use case, ' || sole END
       || ': a goal reached in one use case is a use case, not a journey; remove the journey, or add the steps it is missing.' AS message
FROM counted
WHERE steps > 0 AND use_cases < 2
ORDER BY record

name: lone-child
summary: A group with exactly one child.
explanation: A level that holds one record groups nothing. A group (the `group_name` of every kind that has one, read from the record_group view: terms, UC requirements, view requirements, API requirements, pattern rules, standard rules and a product's own kinds) is counted among its parent's children of one kind, compared trimmed and in any letter case, and reported on that parent. A flow's steps per path and a domain's use cases per their result's aggregate or read model are not read: a path may hold one step, and an aggregate or read model with one use case has nothing to merge with. Merge the group into a neighbor, or give it more.
query:
SELECT m.parent AS record, pk.label || ' ' || m.parent || '''s group "' || m.label
       || '" has only one ' || lower(k.label) || ', ' || m.child || '; merge it into a neighboring group, or give it more.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT r.parent_id AS parent, r.kind, lower(trim(g.label)) AS bucket, min(trim(g.label)) AS label, count(*) AS n, any_value(r.id) AS child
  FROM record_group g JOIN record_parent r ON r.id = g.id
  WHERE r.kind NOT IN ('flow_step', 'use_case')
  GROUP BY r.parent_id, r.kind, lower(trim(g.label))
) m
JOIN record_id p ON p.id = m.parent
JOIN meta_kind pk ON pk.name = p.kind
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = m.kind
WHERE m.n = 1
ORDER BY record, message

name: manual-test-file-silent
summary: A manual test whose file exists but never mentions it.
explanation: A manual test may name a file that holds the steps a person follows. Nothing ties that file to the test until it names the test's ID. Manual tests are not held to the automated rule (test-file-missing-id), so a silent file is a warning. Name the test in the file, or point its `file` at the file that carries it out.
query:
SELECT t.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || t.id || ' names the file ' || t.file || ', but that file does not mention ' || t.id
       || '; name the test in the file, or point its file at the one that carries it out.' AS message
FROM test_run t
JOIN file_facts f ON f.record = t.id
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = t.kind
WHERE t.state = 'manual' AND f.file_exists AND NOT f.contains_id
ORDER BY record

name: not-built
summary: An obligation not every file of what implements it exists for yet, as coverage counts it.
explanation: Coverage counts an obligation as built once every one of the specific technical records that implement it names a file that exists, and there is at least one: a constraint's value type, an invariant's rule, a specification's predicate, a policy's event handler, a domain service's service, a UC requirement's command or query handlers (of what its fulfilling steps invoke) with the predicates and services of what they check, select by or call, and the adapter of each integration its steps exchange with, a view requirement's UI components that build it, an API requirement's endpoint handler, a standard rule's meeting records. Nothing else counts: no data model, unique key or UI component that only renders the view. A pattern rule asks for proof only. This warning names exactly the obligations coverage lists as not built. Add the technical record with its file, or write each file it names.
query: SELECT id AS record, message FROM coverage_gap WHERE missing = 'built' ORDER BY record, domain NULLS LAST

name: not-designed
summary: An obligation whose implementation is not specified yet, as coverage counts it.
explanation: Coverage counts an obligation as designed once its implementation is specified: a UC requirement once a step of its use case's flow fulfills it, a standard rule once a technical record meets it, a product's own obligation once a record links to it with a design relation. A constraint, invariant, specification, policy, domain service, view requirement and API requirement are designed by construction, and a pattern rule wherever it is owed. This warning names exactly the obligations coverage lists as not designed, so the two never disagree. Fulfill the UC requirement from a step of its flow, or link what designs the obligation.
query: SELECT id AS record, message FROM coverage_gap WHERE missing = 'designed' ORDER BY record, domain NULLS LAST

name: not-proved
summary: An obligation no automated or manual test at an allowed level proves yet, as coverage counts it.
explanation: Coverage counts an obligation as proved once a test of it is automated or manual, at a level its test kind allows, and, when automated, its file exists and names the test's ID. A pattern rule is reported once for each domain that owes it, proved there only by its pattern rule test naming that domain. A test not automated yet does not prove, and the message says so. This warning names exactly the obligations coverage lists as not proved. Write the test, automate it or run it by hand, at a level its kind allows.
query: SELECT id AS record, message FROM coverage_gap WHERE missing = 'proved' ORDER BY record, domain NULLS LAST

name: outcome-duration-without-journey
summary: A business outcome whose measure reads as a duration that no journey serves.
explanation: A duration measure, the time from one moment to another, times a journey: the use cases and handoffs, in order, from the trigger its clock starts at to the result it stops at (LA-PRD-UC33-R09). The check reads the measure's words, in any letter case: time, days, hours, minutes or weeks followed by from; how long; median and later from; or from and later to (the words the schema 5 upgrade reads). An outcome so measured that no journey serves is reported. Write the journey it times, its trigger and result first, and link it to the outcome; a duration inside one sitting of one actor is a use case's instead, and a measure that is not a duration is restated.
query:
SELECT o.id AS record,
       'Business outcome ' || o.id || ' measures a duration ("' || trim(o.measure) || '") that no journey serves: write the journey it times, from its trigger to its result, and link it to the outcome, or restate the measure if it is not a duration.' AS message
FROM business_outcome o
WHERE regexp_matches(coalesce(o.measure, ''), '(?i)\b(time|days|hours|minutes|weeks) from\b|\bhow long\b|\bmedian\b.*\bfrom\b|\bfrom\b.+\bto\b')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM serves s JOIN journey j ON j.id = s.source_id WHERE s.target_id = o.id)
ORDER BY record

name: outcome-target-undated
summary: A business outcome whose target says no date by which it is reached.
explanation: An outcome is a change someone would miss, with a measure and a target by a date (LA-STD-MODELING-R13): without a date the target can never be missed, so it measures nothing. The target says by when, as a year (by 2027) or a span from a known event (within six months of the first release, by the end of the first year). Give the target its date with the Business outcome's change command.
query:
SELECT o.id AS record,
       'Business outcome ' || o.id || ' gives its target with no date: say by when it is reached, such as within a year of opening or by 2027.' AS message
FROM business_outcome o
WHERE NOT regexp_matches(o.target, '(?i)\b(within|by|before|until)\b|\b(19|20)[0-9]{2}\b')
ORDER BY record

name: package-not-in-manifest
summary: A record names a package that none of its product's package.json files lists.
explanation: A package_use row says a technical record uses a package, so that every dependency is accounted for by what it serves. Naming a package no manifest lists is a stale or mistyped claim: the package was removed, renamed or never added, and the record no longer tells the truth about the code. Fix the name, add the dependency to the package.json the code runs from, or remove the package_use row.
query:
SELECT u.record_id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || u.record_id || ' names package ' || u.package || ', which no package.json of its product lists.' AS message
FROM package_use u
JOIN record_id r ON r.id = u.record_id
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = r.kind
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM package_facts f WHERE f.package = u.package)
ORDER BY record, u.package

name: pattern-candidate
summary: A pattern's slot with three or more fills, unless it says why its fills vary by design: what they repeat is a pattern candidate.
explanation: A fill is accidental complexity written by hand at a slot, against the slot's contract, and counted as accidental debt. Three fills of one slot are the same decision made three times: what they share can be stated once, in the pattern's fixed part or as a setting, and the code derived from it. One or two fills are not reported, since a pattern drawn from too few examples overfits. A slot whose fills are each its own record's business logic, such as a UI component, says so with the reason its fills vary by design, and is not reported; its page shows the reason. Make the pattern express what the fills repeat and generate them, split the slot where they truly differ, or, when no fill repeats another, give the slot the reason its fills vary by design.
query:
SELECT s.id AS record,
       'Slot ' || s.id || ' (' || s.title || ') has ' || count(*) || ' fills (' || string_agg(f.source_id, ', ' ORDER BY f.source_id)
       || '): a pattern candidate; make the pattern''s fixed part or a setting express what they repeat, and generate them.' AS message
FROM slot s JOIN fills f ON f.target_id = s.id
WHERE s.fills_vary_by_design IS NULL
GROUP BY s.id, s.title
HAVING count(*) >= 3
ORDER BY record

name: pattern-not-followed
summary: A pattern that no use case and no domain follows.
explanation: No domain owes its rules, so they count in no domain's coverage. Link the use cases or domains that follow it with `follows`, or remove the pattern if nothing needs it.
query:
SELECT p.id AS record,
       'No use case or domain follows pattern ' || p.id || ', so '
       || CASE p.rules WHEN 0 THEN 'it is not used anywhere.'
                       WHEN 1 THEN 'its 1 rule is not counted in any domain''s coverage.'
                       ELSE 'its ' || p.rules || ' rules are not counted in any domain''s coverage.' END AS message
FROM (SELECT p.id, (SELECT count(*) FROM pattern_rule r WHERE r.pattern_id = p.id) AS rules FROM pattern p) p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM follows f WHERE f.target_id = p.id)
ORDER BY record

name: pattern-rule-test-outside-followers
summary: A pattern rule test names a domain that follows its pattern.
explanation: A pattern rule test proves its rule in one domain that follows the pattern: the domain itself follows it, or one of its use cases does, and every such domain owes every rule of the pattern. A test naming a domain that does not follow the pattern proves the rule where nothing owes it. Name a domain that follows the pattern, link the domain or its use case to the pattern with `follows`, or remove the test.
query:
SELECT t.id AS record,
       'Pattern rule test ' || t.id || ' proves rule ' || t.pattern_rule_id || ' in domain ' || t.domain_id || ', which does not follow pattern '
       || r.pattern_id || '; name a domain that does, or link ' || t.domain_id || ' or one of its use cases to the pattern with follows.' AS message
FROM pattern_rule_test t
JOIN pattern_rule r ON r.id = t.pattern_rule_id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM owed_pattern_rules o WHERE o.id = t.pattern_rule_id AND o.domain = t.domain_id)
ORDER BY record

name: pattern-setting-missing
summary: A use case that follows a pattern gives each of the pattern's settings.
explanation: Each setting of the pattern (a pattern_setting row) needs a setting_value row from each use case that follows it: the value the use case gives it. A domain that follows a pattern itself owes every rule and gives no settings. Give the missing setting a value.
query:
SELECT f.source_id AS record,
       'Use case ' || f.source_id || ' follows pattern ' || f.target_id || ' but gives no value for its setting "' || s.name
       || '"; give it a value.' AS message
FROM follows f
JOIN use_case u ON u.id = f.source_id
JOIN pattern_setting s ON s.pattern_id = f.target_id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM setting_value v WHERE v.follower_id = f.source_id AND v.pattern_id = f.target_id AND v.setting = s.name)
ORDER BY record, message

name: query-title-verb
summary: A query whose title does not start with Get, List or Find.
explanation: A query asks for data and changes nothing, so its title starts with the verb that says what comes back: Get for one thing, List for several, Find for a search, such as "Get a member's loans", "List overdue loans" or "Find a tool by name". A query titled like a command ("Check the workspace", "Export a theme") reads as a change. Retitle the query with Get, List or Find.
query:
SELECT id AS record,
       'Query ' || id || ' is titled "' || trim(title) || '", which does not start with Get, List or Find; title a query by what it returns, such as "List overdue loans".' AS message
FROM query
WHERE NOT regexp_matches(trim(title), '^(get|list|find)([^a-z]|$)', 'i')
ORDER BY record

name: repository-persists-nothing
summary: A repository that persists no aggregate.
explanation: A repository exists to load and save its aggregate, whole, and says which with its one persists link. One that persists none is a leftover, or its link is missing. Link the aggregate it persists with persists, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'Repository ' || r.id || ' persists no aggregate: link the aggregate it loads and saves with persists, or remove it.' AS message
FROM repository r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM persists p WHERE p.source_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: serves-no-outcome
summary: An aggregate, read model or obligation no business outcome reaches: no use case whose aggregate or read model serves an outcome, and no journey serving one, reaches it.
explanation: Everything in a product serves at least one business outcome (LA-STD-MODELING-R13). A record serves an outcome when a use case whose aggregate or read model serves that outcome, or a journey serving it, reaches it: a use case through its steps, the commands and queries they invoke and what those change, check, call and read, the views they happen in, the endpoints that expose them, the integrations they exchange with and the patterns it follows; a journey through its steps and the use cases and policies they carry out (the Serves reach, LA-TRC-DS06, worked out on every load and never stored). An aggregate, read model or obligation none reaches is built for no one the product exists for: write the use case that needs it, with a step that invokes what reaches it, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || r.id || ' serves no outcome: no use case whose aggregate or read model serves a business outcome, and no journey serving one, reaches it. Write the use case that needs it, or remove it.' AS message
FROM record_id r
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = r.kind
WHERE (k.obligation OR r.kind IN ('aggregate', 'read_model'))
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM record_serves s WHERE s.record = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: specification-title-article
summary: A specification whose title starts with an article: A, An or The.
explanation: A specification is a yes/no condition a record meets or not, and its title names that condition with no article, such as "Tool is available" or "Member in good standing", so a command's or query's list of the specifications it checks reads as a list of conditions. Drop the article from the start of the title.
query:
SELECT id AS record,
       'Specification ' || id || ' is titled "' || trim(title) || '", which starts with "' || regexp_extract(trim(title), '^[A-Za-z]+') || '"; name the condition with no article, such as "Tool is available".' AS message
FROM specification
WHERE regexp_matches(trim(title), '^(a|an|the)\s', 'i')
ORDER BY record

name: specification-unused
summary: A specification that nothing uses.
explanation: A specification has no owner: it exists because commands check it and queries select by it. One that nothing uses is a leftover, or a link is missing. Link the commands that check it or the queries that select by it, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'Specification ' || r.id || ' is used by nothing: commands check it and queries select by it; link the commands that check it or the queries that select by it, or remove it.' AS message
FROM specification r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM checks c WHERE c.target_id = r.id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM selects_by q WHERE q.target_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: step-order
summary: The steps on each path of a flow or a journey are numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on, without gaps.
explanation: A flow's steps, and a journey's, are read in `position` within their `path`, a short name such as main or refused, compared trimmed and in any letter case. The schema gives each step a whole number that no other step on its path has; a path whose positions skip a number is reported once, on the first step after the gap. Renumber the steps of the path to close the gap, or move a step with its move command.
query:
WITH steps AS (
  SELECT id, 'Flow step' AS label, 'flow' AS owner, flow_id AS parent, lower(trim(path)) AS step_path, position AS n FROM flow_step
  UNION ALL
  SELECT id, 'Journey step', 'journey', journey_id, lower(trim(path)), position FROM journey_step
),
paths AS (
  SELECT parent, step_path, max(n) AS top FROM steps GROUP BY parent, step_path
),
gaps AS (
  SELECT p.parent, p.step_path, min(m) AS first_missing, string_agg(m::VARCHAR, ', ' ORDER BY m) AS missing_list
  FROM paths p CROSS JOIN range(1, p.top) t(m)
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM steps x WHERE x.parent = p.parent AND x.step_path = p.step_path AND x.n = t.m)
  GROUP BY p.parent, p.step_path
)
SELECT s.id AS record,
       s.label || ' ' || s.id || ' has position ' || s.n
       || CASE WHEN s.step_path = 'main' THEN '' ELSE ' on path ' || s.step_path END
       || ' in ' || s.owner || ' ' || s.parent || ', but no step'
       || CASE WHEN s.step_path = 'main' THEN '' ELSE ' of that path' END || ' has position ' || g.missing_list
       || '; number the steps of ' || CASE WHEN s.step_path = 'main' THEN 'a ' || s.owner ELSE 'a path' END
       || ' 1, 2, 3 and so on, with no gaps.' AS message
FROM gaps g
JOIN steps s ON s.parent = g.parent AND s.step_path = g.step_path
WHERE s.n = (SELECT min(x.n) FROM steps x WHERE x.parent = g.parent AND x.step_path = g.step_path AND x.n > g.first_missing)
ORDER BY record, message

name: step-repeated-per-interface
summary: Variant steps of one flow, on two or more interfaces, that invoke the same command or query.
explanation: A use case's flow is the same through every interface that offers it: a step says what the actor does or learns, and each interface's version of the flow, derived from the steps, says how that interface carries it out. A variant step is for something only one interface does. Variant steps of two or more interfaces that invoke the same command or query are the same step written once per interface, each naming its interface's mechanism. Make them one step every interface does, saying what the actor does or learns, with the requirements each fulfilled; keep a variant only for what that one interface alone does.
query:
SELECT s.id AS record,
       'Flow step ' || s.id || ', a variant of ' || s.interface_id || ', invokes ' || v.target_id || ', as other interfaces'' variants in its flow ' || s.flow_id || ' do ('
       || string_agg(DISTINCT o.id || ' of ' || o.interface_id, ', ' ORDER BY o.id || ' of ' || o.interface_id)
       || '): the same step written per interface; make them one step every interface does, and let each interface''s version say how.' AS message
FROM flow_step s
JOIN invokes v ON v.source_id = s.id
JOIN flow_step o ON o.flow_id = s.flow_id AND o.interface_id IS NOT NULL AND o.interface_id <> s.interface_id
JOIN invokes w ON w.source_id = o.id AND w.target_id = v.target_id
WHERE s.interface_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.id, s.interface_id, v.target_id, s.flow_id
ORDER BY record

name: step-unreached
summary: A step that invokes a command or query one of the interfaces that offer its use case cannot reach, and that no integration performing its use case carries out.
explanation: A use case's flow is the same through every interface that offers it, and each interface carries a step out through its own means: a web app or desktop in a view that presents the step's command or query (a view of every such interface, or of that one), an API through the endpoint that exposes it, a CLI or agent tools through a record of the product's own interface design kinds under it (such as Lathe's CLI commands) or that presents it (such as an invocation that carries out several commands and queries; one that sits under an interface reaches only that one, any other every CLI and agent tools of its product). So each interface that offers the use case must reach what each step invokes, but for a step that is another interface's variant, and a step that exchanges with an integration that performs the use case: the outside system carries that step out on its own. An interface of kind other reaches its operations in a way no record says, so it is not read. Have a view present the command or query, add the endpoint, or the product's own record under it or that presents it, make the step a variant of the interfaces that do reach it, or stop offering the use case through that interface.
query:
WITH carried AS (
  SELECT s.id AS step, v.target_id AS operation, i.id AS interface, i.kind
  FROM flow_step s
  JOIN flow f ON f.id = s.flow_id
  JOIN offers o ON o.target_id = f.use_case_id
  JOIN interface i ON i.id = o.source_id
  JOIN invokes v ON v.source_id = s.id
  WHERE (s.interface_id IS NULL OR s.interface_id = i.id) AND i.kind <> 'other'
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM exchanges_with x JOIN performs p ON p.source_id = x.target_id WHERE x.source_id = s.id AND p.target_id = f.use_case_id)
)
SELECT c.step AS record,
       'Flow step ' || c.step || ' invokes ' || c.operation || ', but ' || c.interface || ', an interface of kind ' || c.kind || ' that offers its use case, has no '
       || CASE WHEN c.kind IN ('web app', 'desktop') THEN 'view that presents it' WHEN c.kind = 'API' THEN 'endpoint that exposes it' ELSE 'record of the product''s own interface design under it or that presents it' END
       || '; add one, or make the step a variant of the interfaces that reach it.' AS message
FROM carried c
WHERE NOT CASE
  WHEN c.kind IN ('web app', 'desktop') THEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM presents p JOIN view w ON w.id = p.source_id WHERE p.target_id = c.operation AND (w.interface_id IS NULL OR w.interface_id = c.interface))
  WHEN c.kind = 'API' THEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM endpoint e WHERE e.command_id = c.operation OR e.query_id = c.operation)
  ELSE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM record_parent p JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = p.kind WHERE p.parent_id = c.operation AND k.product_id IS NOT NULL AND k.stage = 'interface-design' AND NOT k.obligation)
    OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM presents p JOIN record_id r ON r.id = p.source_id JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = r.kind
               WHERE p.target_id = c.operation AND k.product_id IS NOT NULL AND k.stage = 'interface-design' AND NOT k.obligation
                 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM record_parent u JOIN interface o ON o.id = u.parent_id WHERE u.id = p.source_id AND u.parent_id <> c.interface))
END
ORDER BY record, c.interface

name: table-schema-mismatch
summary: A table kept in a database whose file does not define it as the spec says: its name, a column or a key.
explanation: A table, view or materialized view that names a file is checked against that file read as text (a migration, a SQL schema, or code that creates it): the file defines a table or view of its name; every column its entity's or read model's fields give (a field's column_name, else its name in lower case with underscores; a value object of several fields flattened into its fields' columns; an entity's table also holds the fields of the children kept in its root's table); and each primary, unique and foreign key by its columns, a foreign key also by its target table. It recognizes CREATE TABLE and CREATE VIEW (OR REPLACE, TEMP, MATERIALIZED, IF NOT EXISTS) with their column definitions and inline or table PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE and REFERENCES, the columns an AS SELECT body selects or names with AS, CREATE UNIQUE INDEX and ALTER TABLE ... ADD. It does not compare types, NOT NULL, CHECKs, a unique key's name or condition, or index keys, and it cannot see a statement built at run time from pieces the text does not show. A missing file is technical-file-missing instead. Change the file to match, or the spec when the file is right.
query:
SELECT f.record,
       'Table ' || f.record || ' names ' || f.file || ', which '
       || CASE f.part
            WHEN 'table' THEN 'defines no table or view named ' || f.expected
            WHEN 'column' THEN 'gives ' || f.name || ' no column ' || f.expected
            ELSE 'gives ' || f.name || ' no ' || f.part || ' key ' || f.expected
          END || '.' AS message
FROM table_facts f
WHERE NOT f.found
ORDER BY f.record, CASE f.part WHEN 'table' THEN 1 WHEN 'column' THEN 2 WHEN 'primary' THEN 3 WHEN 'unique' THEN 4 ELSE 5 END, f.expected

name: technical-file-missing
summary: A technical record whose file does not exist yet.
explanation: The technical specification may name a file before it is written, so this is work to do, not breakage: until the file exists, what the record implements is not built. A technical record's file may be a file or a folder of files under the product root. Write the file, or fix the path (relative to the product root).
query:
SELECT f.record,
       k.label || ' ' || f.record || ' names ' || f.file || ', which does not exist yet.' AS message
FROM file_facts f
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = f.kind
WHERE NOT f.file_exists AND f.kind NOT IN (SELECT kind FROM test_level_allowed) AND f.kind <> 'test_data_set'
ORDER BY record

name: term-used-unlinked
summary: A term's meaning uses another term of its product by title without a builds_on link to it.
explanation: Definitions build up, never in a circle (LA-STD-MODELING-R12): a term is defined only by plain words and terms below it, and names each one it uses with builds_on, so the store can refuse a loop. The check reads each meaning in lower case, with text in backticks left out as code, and looks for every other term of the product by title as a whole word, singular or plural (a title ending in a consonant and y also as -ies); a shorter title found only inside a longer term's title (Domain inside Domain event) does not count. It cannot tell a word used in another sense, so it is a warning. Link the term with builds_on to the term it uses, or say it in plain words.
query:
WITH term_in AS (
  SELECT t.id, t.title, s.product_id,
         lower(regexp_replace(t.meaning, '`[^`]*`', ' ', 'g')) AS meaning,
         CASE WHEN regexp_matches(lower(trim(t.title)), '[^aeiou]y$')
              THEN regexp_replace(left(lower(trim(t.title)), -1), '([.*+?^$(){}|\[\]\\])', '\\\1', 'g') || '(y|ies)'
              ELSE regexp_replace(lower(trim(t.title)), '([.*+?^$(){}|\[\]\\])', '\\\1', 'g') || '(s|es)?' END AS word,
         regexp_extract(lower(trim(t.title)), '[a-z0-9]+') AS run,
         regexp_matches(lower(trim(t.title)), '^[^a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9]+$') AS alone,
         regexp_matches(lower(trim(t.title)), '[^aeiou]y$') AS ies
  FROM term t
  JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = t.id
),
keyed AS (
  SELECT id, product_id, title, word,
         unnest(CASE WHEN run = '' THEN [NULL]
                     WHEN NOT alone THEN [run]
                     WHEN ies THEN [run, left(run, -1) || 'ies']
                     ELSE [run, run || 's', run || 'es'] END) AS key
  FROM term_in
),
meaning_word AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT id, product_id, title, meaning, unnest(regexp_split_to_array(meaning, '[^a-z0-9]+')) AS token FROM term_in
),
title_word AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT id, product_id, title, word, unnest(regexp_split_to_array(lower(title), '[^a-z0-9]+')) AS token FROM term_in
),
used AS (
  SELECT w.id AS a_id, w.title AS a_title, w.meaning, k.id AS b_id, k.title AS b_title, k.word
  FROM keyed k JOIN meaning_word w ON w.token = k.key AND w.product_id = k.product_id
  WHERE w.id <> k.id AND regexp_matches(w.meaning, '(^|[^a-z0-9])' || k.word || '($|[^a-z0-9])')
  UNION
  SELECT w.id, w.title, w.meaning, k.id, k.title, k.word
  FROM keyed k JOIN meaning_word w ON w.product_id = k.product_id
  WHERE k.key IS NULL AND w.id <> k.id AND regexp_matches(w.meaning, '(^|[^a-z0-9])' || k.word || '($|[^a-z0-9])')
),
longer AS (
  SELECT b_id AS id, string_agg(c_word, '|' ORDER BY length(c_title) DESC, c_id) AS words
  FROM (
    SELECT u.b_id, w.id AS c_id, w.title AS c_title, w.word AS c_word, u.word AS b_word
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT b_id, b_title, word FROM used) u
    JOIN keyed k ON k.id = u.b_id
    JOIN title_word w ON w.token = k.key AND w.product_id = k.product_id
    WHERE w.id <> u.b_id AND length(w.title) > length(u.b_title)
    UNION
    SELECT u.b_id, w.id, w.title, w.word, u.word
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT b_id, b_title, word FROM used) u
    JOIN keyed k ON k.id = u.b_id
    JOIN title_word w ON w.product_id = k.product_id
    WHERE k.key IS NULL AND w.id <> u.b_id AND length(w.title) > length(u.b_title)
  )
  WHERE regexp_matches(lower(c_title), '(^|[^a-z0-9])' || b_word || '($|[^a-z0-9])')
  GROUP BY b_id
)
SELECT u.a_id AS record,
       'Term ' || u.a_id || ' (' || u.a_title || ') uses "' || u.b_title || '" in its meaning but does not build on ' || u.b_id
       || ': link it with builds_on, or say it in plain words.' AS message
FROM used u
LEFT JOIN longer l ON l.id = u.b_id
WHERE regexp_matches(
        CASE WHEN l.words IS NULL THEN u.meaning
             ELSE regexp_replace(u.meaning, '(^|[^a-z0-9])(' || l.words || ')($|[^a-z0-9])', '\1 \3', 'g') END,
        '(^|[^a-z0-9])' || u.word || '($|[^a-z0-9])')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM builds_on k WHERE k.source_id = u.a_id AND k.target_id = u.b_id)
ORDER BY record, u.b_id

name: test-case-unnamed
summary: A test case in the product's test files names a test whose file it is in, so every test in the code leads back to the record it proves.
explanation: test-file-missing-id follows a test record to its code; this check follows the code back. The engine reads the product's test files (those matching the tests globs in lathe.config.json, by default **/*.test.{ts,tsx,js,mjs} and **/*.spec.{ts,tsx,js}, never in node_modules, dist or another product's folder, and every file a test record names) as text and finds each test case: a call of it or test, with its modifiers and each forms, whose name is a string or template literal, inside the describe calls around it. A test case must name, in its own name, its describes' names or its each rows, the ID of a test (or of a product kind's record that proves an obligation) whose file is the file it is in. One that names none proves nothing anyone can find. Start its name, or its describe's, with the ID of the test it proves, adding that test when the spec lacks it, or remove the test case if it proves nothing.
query:
SELECT NULL AS record,
       c.file || ':' || c.line || ': the test case "' || c.name || '" names no test whose file is ' || c.file
       || '; start its name, or its describe''s, with the ID of the test it proves, or remove it if it proves nothing.' AS message
FROM test_case c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM test_case_id i JOIN file_facts f ON f.record = i.id
  WHERE i.file = c.file AND i.position = c.position AND f.path = c.file
    AND (f.kind IN (SELECT kind FROM test_level_allowed)
      -- A record of a product's own kind that proves an obligation stands in for a test.
      OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM link l JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation AND r.role = 'proof' WHERE l.source_id = f.record)))
ORDER BY c.file, c.position

name: test-data-set-file-missing
summary: A test data set whose file does not exist.
explanation: A test data set's file is the seed or fixture that builds it, a file or a folder of files under the product root. When an automated test starts from it, a missing file means that test cannot run, so it is an error. Otherwise the plan may name the file before it is written, so it is a warning. Write the file, or fix the path (relative to the product root).
query:
SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM starts_from s JOIN test_run t ON t.id = s.source_id WHERE s.target_id = f.record AND t.state = 'automated') THEN 'error' ELSE 'warning' END AS severity,
       f.record,
       'Test data set ' || f.record || ' names ' || f.file || ', which does not exist'
       || CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM starts_from s JOIN test_run t ON t.id = s.source_id WHERE s.target_id = f.record AND t.state = 'automated') THEN ', so the automated tests that start from it cannot run.' ELSE ' yet.' END AS message
FROM file_facts f
WHERE f.kind = 'test_data_set' AND NOT f.file_exists
ORDER BY record

name: test-data-set-unused
summary: A test data set that no test starts from.
explanation: A test data set exists because tests start from it: it is prepared before them and reset after. One that no test starts from is a leftover, or a link is missing. Link the tests that start from it with starts_from, or remove it.
query:
SELECT d.id AS record, 'Test data set ' || d.id || ' is used by nothing: tests start from it; link the tests that start from it with starts_from, or remove it.' AS message
FROM test_data_set d
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM starts_from s WHERE s.target_id = d.id)
ORDER BY record

name: test-file-missing
summary: A test's `file` exists, and so does that of a product kind's record that proves an obligation.
explanation: For an automated or manual test a missing file is an error. A test that is not automated yet may name the file it will live in, so for it a missing file is a warning. The file must be a file under the product root, never a folder. A record of a product's own kind that proves an obligation and names a file is checked as an automated test is. Fix the path (relative to the product root), or write the file.
query:
SELECT CASE WHEN t.state = 'not automated yet' THEN 'warning' ELSE 'error' END AS severity, t.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || t.id || ' names the file ' || t.file || ', which does not exist'
       || CASE WHEN t.state = 'not automated yet' THEN ' yet.' ELSE '.' END AS message
FROM test_run t
JOIN file_facts f ON f.record = t.id
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = t.kind
WHERE NOT f.file_exists
UNION ALL
-- A record of a product's own kind that proves an obligation stands in for a test, and its file is checked as one.
SELECT 'error', f.record, k.label || ' ' || f.record || ' names the file ' || f.file || ', which does not exist.'
FROM file_facts f JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = f.kind
WHERE k.product_id IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM link l JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation AND r.role = 'proof' WHERE l.source_id = f.record) AND NOT f.file_exists
ORDER BY record

name: test-file-missing-id
summary: An automated test's file names the test, and so does that of a product kind's record that proves an obligation, so the code can be traced back to it.
explanation: A test proves exactly its parent, and its file names the test's own ID as a whole ID (TL-LEND-INV01-T, not inside TL-LEND-INV01-T2), so a reader of the code finds the record and a reader of the record finds the code. Until it does, the test proves nothing. A missing file is test-file-missing instead; manual tests and tests not automated yet are not checked here. A record of a product's own kind that proves an obligation and names a file is held to the same rule, since it counts as proof only when its file names it. Put the test's ID in the test's name in the file.
query:
SELECT t.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || t.id || ' names the file ' || t.file || ', but that file does not mention ' || t.id
       || '; put the ID in the test''s name in the file.' AS message
FROM test_run t
JOIN file_facts f ON f.record = t.id
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = t.kind
WHERE t.state = 'automated' AND f.file_exists AND NOT f.contains_id
UNION ALL
-- A record of a product's own kind that proves an obligation stands in for a test, and its file must name it as one's must.
SELECT f.record,
       k.label || ' ' || f.record || ' names the file ' || f.file || ', but that file does not mention ' || f.record
       || '; put the ID in the test''s name in the file.'
FROM file_facts f JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = f.kind
WHERE k.product_id IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM link l JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation AND r.role = 'proof' WHERE l.source_id = f.record) AND f.file_exists AND NOT f.contains_id
ORDER BY record

name: test-level-not-allowed
summary: A test whose run by level its test kind does not allow.
explanation: A test's level says only how it runs, cheapest first: unit (in process, no storage or I/O), integration (in process, with real storage: a database, files, git), service (through the product's interface in process, with real storage), system (the running product driven from outside through its real interface) and browser (a real browser or the desktop shell against the running app); a manual test names the level a person exercises. Each test kind is run at the levels that can prove what it tests, and a test runs at the lowest of them that can observe its result: a constraint test at unit or integration (a constraint enforced by a SQL CHECK can only be tested against the database); an invariant or specification test at unit or integration; a domain service test at unit; a policy test at integration, service or system, or at browser where only the running app shows the reaction; a use case test at service, system or browser; a view test at unit or browser; an endpoint test at service or system; a flow test at system or browser (and at the one that fits its flow's interface, flow-test-level-for-interface); an integration test at integration, service or system; a pattern rule or standard rule test at any level. A test at another level proves nothing in coverage. Run the test at an allowed level and set its level, or make it the test kind of what it really proves.
query:
SELECT t.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || t.id || ' runs at level ' || t.level || ', which a ' || lower(k.label) || ' does not allow; run it at '
       || (SELECT string_agg(a.level::VARCHAR, ', ' ORDER BY a.level) FROM test_level_allowed a WHERE a.kind = t.kind) || '.' AS message
FROM test_run t
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = t.kind
WHERE NOT t.level_allowed
ORDER BY record

name: test-title-not-a-result
summary: A test titled by what it does or ought to do, starting with "Tests that" or "Should", rather than by the result it shows.
explanation: A test's title is the observable result it shows, one short sentence that is true when the test passes, such as "An overdue loan is refused a renewal": a reader of the test plan learns what holds without opening the test. A title that starts with "Tests that", "Test that", "Tests whether", "Tests if" or "Should" says what the test checks or hopes for instead. A title that only starts with the noun "Tests", such as "Tests run in order", is not read. Rewrite the title as the result.
query:
WITH titled AS (
  SELECT 'Constraint test' AS label, id, title FROM constraint_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Invariant test' AS label, id, title FROM invariant_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Specification test' AS label, id, title FROM specification_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Policy test' AS label, id, title FROM policy_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Domain service test' AS label, id, title FROM domain_service_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Use case test' AS label, id, title FROM use_case_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'View test' AS label, id, title FROM view_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Endpoint test' AS label, id, title FROM endpoint_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Flow test' AS label, id, title FROM flow_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Integration test' AS label, id, title FROM integration_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Pattern rule test' AS label, id, title FROM pattern_rule_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Standard rule test' AS label, id, title FROM standard_rule_test
)
SELECT id AS record,
       label || ' ' || id || ' is titled "' || trim(title) || '", which says what it tests or should do; title a test by the result it shows, such as "An overdue loan is refused a renewal".' AS message
FROM titled
WHERE regexp_matches(lower(trim(title)), '^(should|it should|tests? (that|whether|if))([^a-z]|$)')
ORDER BY record

name: title-breaks-convention
summary: A use case or journey title that breaks its naming convention: an interface named in it, a list in a journey, or a journey's CRUD verb over a record.
explanation: A use case is named for its result, verb first, two to six words: a command use case with its command's verb (Borrow a tool), which use-case-title-off-result reads, and a query use case for the question (See the tools waiting for repair). A journey is named the same way for the summary goal its steps reach together, verb first, such as Get a damaged tool back in lending. Neither names a screen, a tool or a technology: a use case happens through interfaces, with one flow each, so the interface belongs to its flows, not its title, and a journey's steps are use cases.
