The check reads only the mechanical parts, in any letter case and as whole words: a use case or journey title that holds one of its product's interface titles or the words command line, CLI, desktop app, web app, MCP, API, agent tools, command layer or page (or their plurals); a journey title that holds a list, a comma followed later by "and" or "or"; and a journey title that starts with a CRUD verb (create, read, update, delete, change or edit) and holds the word record, records or data, since a journey names the domain's own verb for its goal (Get a damaged tool back in lending), never a verb over a record or data; a command use case's verb is its command's (Change a check). A journey strings goals, so its "and" with no comma is not read, nor is a journey title that does not start with a verb. Rename the use case or journey by the convention.
query:
WITH titled AS (
  SELECT 'Use case' AS label, u.id, u.title, s.product_id FROM use_case u JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = u.id
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Journey', j.id, j.title, j.product_id FROM journey j
),
words AS (
  SELECT label, id, title, product_id,
         ' ' || trim(regexp_replace(lower(title), '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g')) || ' ' AS padded,
         split_part(trim(regexp_replace(lower(title), '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g')), ' ', 1) AS first_word
  FROM titled
),
found AS (
  SELECT label, id, title,
         coalesce(
           (SELECT min(n.name) FROM (
              SELECT trim(regexp_replace(lower(i.title), '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g')) AS name FROM interface i WHERE i.product_id = w.product_id
            ) n
            WHERE n.name <> '' AND contains(w.padded, ' ' || n.name || ' ')),
           nullif(regexp_extract(w.padded, ' (command lines?|clis?|desktop apps?|web apps?|mcp|apis?|agent tools?|command layers?|pages?) ', 1), '')
         ) AS interface_word,
         label = 'Journey' AND contains(title, ',') AND regexp_matches(lower(substr(title, strpos(title, ','))), '[^a-z](and|or)([^a-z]|$)') AS lists,
         CASE WHEN label = 'Journey' AND list_contains(string_split('create read update delete change edit', ' '), first_word)
                   AND regexp_matches(padded, ' (records?|data) ')
              THEN first_word END AS crud_verb
  FROM words w
)
SELECT id AS record,
       label || ' ' || id || ' is titled "' || trim(title) || '", which '
       || concat_ws('; it ',
            CASE WHEN interface_word IS NOT NULL THEN 'names an interface or mechanism ("' || interface_word || '")' END,
            CASE WHEN lists THEN 'holds a list (a comma, then "and" or "or")' END,
            CASE WHEN crud_verb IS NOT NULL THEN 'uses the CRUD verb "' || crud_verb || '" over a record or data, not the domain''s own verb' END)
       || CASE WHEN label = 'Use case'
               THEN '; name a use case for one goal of its actor, verb first, such as "Borrow a tool", and leave the interface to its flows.'
               ELSE '; name a journey for the goal its steps reach together, verb first, such as "Get a damaged tool back in lending", and leave the interface to its use cases'' flows.' END AS message
FROM found
WHERE interface_word IS NOT NULL OR lists OR crud_verb IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY record

name: too-many-children
summary: A record with more children of one kind than its product's max_children setting.
explanation: The setting is the product's product_setting row (15 when it has none). A parent with that many children of one kind is missing a level between them, such as another aggregate. It counts a parent's children of each kind of the five design stages, discovery to the technical specification, since those are read as lists under their parent; a test is read under what it proves. Children are also counted per group, read from the record_group view, since each group reads under its own heading: a flow's steps per path, since each path reads as its own list; a domain's use cases per group, their result's aggregate or read model, since each is listed under it; and the records of every kind with a `group_name` (terms, UC requirements, view requirements, API requirements, pattern rules, standard rules and a product's own kinds) per `group_name`; the ungrouped ones are one list. Paths and groups are compared trimmed and in any letter case. Add a level, or a group, and move the children into it; for use cases, split the aggregate or read model.
query:
WITH children AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.kind, p.parent_id, coalesce(g.label, '') AS label
  FROM record_parent p
  JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = p.kind
  LEFT JOIN record_group g ON g.id = p.id
  WHERE p.parent_id IS NOT NULL AND k.stage IS DISTINCT FROM 'test-plan'
),
counted AS (
  SELECT parent_id, kind, lower(trim(label)) AS bucket, min(trim(label)) AS label, count(*) AS n
  FROM children GROUP BY parent_id, kind, lower(trim(label))
)
SELECT c.parent_id AS record,
       pk.label || ' ' || c.parent_id || ' has ' || c.n || ' children of kind ' || c.kind
       || CASE WHEN c.kind = 'flow_step' AND c.bucket <> 'main' THEN ' on path ' || c.label
               WHEN c.kind = 'use_case' AND c.bucket <> '' THEN ' sitting with ' || c.label
               WHEN c.kind <> 'flow_step' AND c.bucket <> '' THEN ' in group ' || c.label ELSE '' END
       || ', more than the ' || coalesce(ps.max_children, 15)
       || ' that the product''s max_children setting allows; '
       || CASE WHEN c.kind = 'use_case' THEN 'split the aggregate or read model they sit with.' ELSE 'add a level between them, such as another aggregate.' END AS message
FROM counted c
JOIN record_id p ON p.id = c.parent_id
JOIN meta_kind pk ON pk.name = p.kind
JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = c.parent_id
LEFT JOIN product_setting ps ON ps.product_id = s.product_id
WHERE c.n > coalesce(ps.max_children, 15)
ORDER BY record, message

name: ui-component-unused
summary: A ui component that nothing uses.
explanation: A ui component has no owner: it exists because it renders views. One that nothing uses is a leftover, or a link is missing. Link the views it renders with renders, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'UI component ' || r.id || ' is used by nothing: it renders views; link the views it renders with renders, or remove it.' AS message
FROM ui_component r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM renders x WHERE x.source_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: use-case-identity-taken
summary: Two use cases of a product with the same first actor and the same result.
explanation: A use case is one role invoking one command, or asking one query, so its identity is its first actor and its result (LA-STD-MODELING-R15): no two use cases of a product share both. Two that do are one use case written twice. The check reports the later ID, naming the earliest. Merge them: move the later one's requirements, steps and tests into the earlier and remove it. A write that adds a use case or an actor, or changes a result, so that two share both, is refused; data already written is reported here. Two use cases with the same result and different first actors are two use cases.
query:
WITH firsts AS (
  SELECT u.id, u.result_id, a.role_name, s.product_id
  FROM use_case u
  JOIN use_case_actor a ON a.use_case_id = u.id AND a.position = 1
  JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = u.id
)
SELECT b.id AS record,
       'Use case ' || b.id || ' has the same first actor (' || b.role_name || ') and result (' || b.result_id || ') as ' || min(a.id)
       || ': no two use cases of a product share both; merge ' || b.id || ' into ' || min(a.id) || '.' AS message
FROM firsts b
JOIN firsts a ON a.product_id = b.product_id AND a.role_name = b.role_name AND a.result_id = b.result_id AND a.id < b.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.role_name, b.result_id
ORDER BY record

name: use-case-invokes-another-command
summary: A flow step that invokes a command other than its use case's result.
explanation: A use case is one role invoking one command, or asking one query: its result (LA-STD-MODELING-R15). So the only command its flow invokes is its result, on any path (main, alternate or refused), in any interface's variant, and whoever the step's subject is; its other steps only ask queries or invoke nothing, and a query use case invokes no command at all. The check reads every step of every flow with an invokes link to a command that is not its use case's result. A second command is a second use case, strung to this one in a journey when one waits on the other, or the command of a policy when the product does it on its own. A write that adds such a link, or changes a result so a step has one, is refused; data already written is reported here.
query:
SELECT s.id AS record,
       'Flow step ' || s.id || ' of ' || u.id || ' invokes the command ' || c.id || ' (' || trim(c.title) || '), but the use case''s result is ' || u.result_id
       || ': a use case invokes no command but its result; make ' || c.id || ' its own use case, joined to this one in a journey, or the command of a policy.' AS message
FROM use_case u
JOIN flow f ON f.use_case_id = u.id
JOIN flow_step s ON s.flow_id = f.id
JOIN invokes i ON i.source_id = s.id
JOIN command c ON c.id = i.target_id
WHERE c.id <> u.result_id
ORDER BY record

name: use-case-not-done
summary: A query use case whose main path's last step that invokes anything asks something other than its result.
explanation: A use case is done when its result is invoked (LA-STD-MODELING-R15). A command use case is done when its main path invokes its result, and the steps after it may only ask queries, such as one confirming the result: a command after it is use-case-invokes-another-command's. A query use case is done when it asks its result, so through each interface that offers it, the main path's last step that invokes anything asks the result. The main path is read per interface version: the steps every interface takes and that interface's own variants, or all the steps when no interface offers the use case; the last step is the one with the highest position. A version whose main path never asks the result is use-case-result-not-invoked's. Unlink the steps after the result, make them a use case of their own, or name as the result the query the use case really ends in.
query:
WITH version AS (
  SELECT o.target_id AS use_case_id, o.source_id AS interface_id FROM offers o
  UNION ALL
  SELECT u.id, NULL FROM use_case u WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offers o WHERE o.target_id = u.id)
),
main AS (
  SELECT f.use_case_id, s.id, s.position, s.interface_id, i.target_id
  FROM flow f JOIN flow_step s ON s.flow_id = f.id LEFT JOIN invokes i ON i.source_id = s.id
  WHERE lower(trim(s.path)) = 'main'
),
last_step AS (
  SELECT v.use_case_id, v.interface_id, arg_max(m.id, m.position) AS step, arg_max(m.target_id, m.position) AS target
  FROM version v JOIN main m ON m.use_case_id = v.use_case_id AND (v.interface_id IS NULL OR m.interface_id IS NULL OR m.interface_id = v.interface_id)
  WHERE m.target_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY v.use_case_id, v.interface_id
)
SELECT u.id AS record,
       'Use case ' || u.id || ' asks its result ' || u.result_id || ', but the last step of its main path that invokes anything'
       || coalesce(' through ' || string_agg(l.interface_id, ', ' ORDER BY l.interface_id), '') || ', ' || min(l.step) || ', invokes ' || min(l.target)
       || ': a query use case is done when it asks its result; unlink the steps after it, make them a use case of their own, or make ' || min(l.target) || ' the result.' AS message
FROM last_step l
JOIN use_case u ON u.id = l.use_case_id
JOIN query q ON q.id = u.result_id
WHERE l.target <> u.result_id
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM main m WHERE m.use_case_id = l.use_case_id AND (l.interface_id IS NULL OR m.interface_id IS NULL OR m.interface_id = l.interface_id) AND m.target_id = u.result_id)
GROUP BY u.id, u.result_id
ORDER BY record

name: use-case-result-in-domain
summary: A use case in a domain other than its result's.
explanation: A use case sits with its result (LA-STD-MODELING-R20): with the aggregate of its result command, or the read model of its result query, in that record's domain. That aggregate or read model is where the use case is listed, worked out from the result and never stored. A use case in another domain would be listed in one domain under another domain's aggregate or read model, and its domain would no longer be the vertical slice that owns its use cases. The check reads each use case whose domain is not its result's aggregate's or read model's domain. Move it to that domain with Move a use case, or give it a result of its own domain. A write that adds a use case, or changes its domain or result, so that its result is of another domain, is refused; data already written is reported here.
query:
SELECT u.id AS record,
       'Use case ' || u.id || ' is in ' || u.domain_id || ', but its result ' || u.result_id || ' is of ' || g.domain_id || ' (its ' || lower(k.label) || ' ' || s.group_id || ')'
       || ': move it to ' || g.domain_id || ' with Move a use case, or give it a result of its own domain.' AS message
FROM use_case u
JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = u.id
JOIN record_scope g ON g.id = s.group_id
JOIN record_id r ON r.id = s.group_id
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = r.kind
WHERE g.domain_id IS DISTINCT FROM u.domain_id
ORDER BY record

name: use-case-result-not-invoked
summary: A use case whose main path, through some interface that offers it, never invokes its result.
explanation: A use case is done when its result is invoked (LA-STD-MODELING-R15), so through each interface that offers it, a step of its main path invokes the result. The main path is read per interface version: the steps every interface takes and that interface's own variants, or all the steps when no interface offers the use case. A path is compared trimmed and in any letter case. A use case with no flow, or a flow with no main path, is left to the use-case-without-flow and flow-without-main-path gaps. Link the main-path step where the actor invokes the result, or name as the result the operation the use case really ends in.
query:
WITH version AS (
  SELECT o.target_id AS use_case_id, o.source_id AS interface_id FROM offers o
  UNION ALL
  SELECT u.id, NULL FROM use_case u WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offers o WHERE o.target_id = u.id)
),
main AS (
  SELECT f.use_case_id, s.id, s.position, s.interface_id, i.target_id
  FROM flow f JOIN flow_step s ON s.flow_id = f.id LEFT JOIN invokes i ON i.source_id = s.id
  WHERE lower(trim(s.path)) = 'main'
),
missed AS (
  SELECT v.use_case_id, v.interface_id FROM version v JOIN use_case u ON u.id = v.use_case_id
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM main m WHERE m.use_case_id = v.use_case_id)
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM main m WHERE m.use_case_id = v.use_case_id AND (v.interface_id IS NULL OR m.interface_id IS NULL OR m.interface_id = v.interface_id) AND m.target_id = u.result_id)
)
SELECT u.id AS record,
       'Use case ' || u.id || ' has ' || u.result_id || ' as its result, but no step of its main path'
       || coalesce(' through ' || string_agg(m.interface_id, ', ' ORDER BY m.interface_id), '')
       || ' invokes it: link the main-path step that invokes it, or make the use case''s result what its main path invokes.' AS message
FROM missed m JOIN use_case u ON u.id = m.use_case_id
GROUP BY u.id, u.result_id
ORDER BY record

name: use-case-title-off-result
summary: A command use case whose title does not start with its command's verb.
explanation: A command use case's title starts with its command's verb (LA-STD-MODELING-R15, LA-STD-NAMING-R02): Borrow a tool, for the command Borrow a tool. The check compares the first word of the use case's title with the first word of its result's title, trimmed and in any letter case. A query use case is titled for the question, with a verb of its own, and is not read. Retitle the use case with its command's verb, or rename the command when its verb is the one that is off.
query:
WITH titled AS (
  SELECT u.id, trim(u.title) AS title, c.id AS command, trim(c.title) AS command_title,
         split_part(lower(trim(u.title)), ' ', 1) AS verb, split_part(lower(trim(c.title)), ' ', 1) AS command_verb
  FROM use_case u JOIN command c ON c.id = u.result_id
)
SELECT id AS record,
       'Use case ' || id || ' is titled "' || title || '", but its result ' || command || ' is "' || command_title
       || '": a command use case starts with its command''s verb; start its title with "' || split_part(command_title, ' ', 1) || '", or rename the command.' AS message
FROM titled
WHERE verb <> command_verb
ORDER BY record

name: value-object-unused
summary: A value object that nothing uses.
explanation: A value object has no owner: it exists because fields of entities, value objects, events or read models are typed with it. One that nothing uses is a leftover, or a link is missing. Type the fields that hold it with it, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'Value object ' || r.id || ' is used by nothing: fields of entities, value objects, events or read models are typed with it; type the fields that hold it with it, or remove it.' AS message
FROM value_object r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM entity_field f WHERE f.type_value_object_id = r.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM value_object_field f WHERE f.type_value_object_id = r.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM event_field f WHERE f.type_value_object_id = r.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM read_model_field f WHERE f.type_value_object_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: variant-not-offered
summary: A variant step whose interface does not offer its use case.
explanation: A step only one interface can do names that interface, and that interface's version of the flow is the only one that has it. An interface that does not offer the use case has no version, so the step would be in none. Offer the use case through the interface, name another interface that does, or make the step every interface's.
query:
SELECT s.id AS record,
       'Flow step ' || s.id || ' is a variant of ' || s.interface_id || ', which does not offer its use case ' || f.use_case_id || '; offer it there, or name an interface that does.' AS message
FROM flow_step s
JOIN flow f ON f.id = s.flow_id
WHERE s.interface_id IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offers o WHERE o.source_id = s.interface_id AND o.target_id = f.use_case_id)
ORDER BY record

name: view-route-not-in-file
summary: A view whose route no file of the UI components that render it names.
explanation: A view's route is the address it is shown at, and the UI components that render it show it there, so one of their files names the route, written any way routes are written (`/tools/{toolId}`, `/tools/:toolId`, `/tools/<tool-id>`, `/tools/[toolId]`, a template's `${toolId}`, or a regular expression literal that matches it, such as `/^\/tools\/(\d+)$/`), in code, a string or a comment. Parameters match whatever their names, and only the path counts: a query string or fragment is not part of a route. Then a reader of the record finds the code, and an address changed on one side and not the other is caught. A view with no route, or whose components' files do not exist yet, is not checked. Correct the view's route, or name it in the file of the component that shows the view at that address.
query:
SELECT r.record,
       'View ' || r.record || ' is at ' || r.route || ', but no file of the UI components that render it (' || r.files
       || ') names that route; correct the view''s route, or name it in the file of the component that shows the view there.' AS message
FROM route_facts r
WHERE r.kind = 'view' AND r.files <> '' AND NOT r.found
ORDER BY record

name: view-unused
summary: A view that presents no command or query.
explanation: A view has no owner: it exists because a person sends commands or asks queries in it, so a step that invokes one is carried out there on a web app or desktop interface. One that presents nothing is a leftover, or a link is missing. Link what it presents with presents, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'View ' || r.id || ' presents no command or query; link what a person sends or asks in it with presents, or remove it.' AS message
FROM view r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM presents p WHERE p.source_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record
